about: The surroundings' shared vectors (brief v0.6.0-04, design §1, which amends brief M4-02's rule; the game's reader is brief v0.6.0-08): tests/shared/surroundings_fixture/ is a synthetic world (origin E 2618250 / N 1101750, height_offset_m 1250.25, the owner's axes, area 'fixture' E 2616000-2625000, N 1095000-1107000: 9 km x 12 km) and nine synthetic swissALTIRegio tiles at a 1000 m cell (source.json; invented heights in whole centimetres, no swisstopo data). surroundings.json (schema 2) grows the area by margin_m 3000 at spacing_m 3000: the box E 2613000-2628000, N 1092000-1110000, 6 columns x 7 rows, rows north to south, columns west to east; vertex (row r, column c) is LV95 (e_min + 3000 c, n_max - 3000 r), local x = E - 2618250, z = -(N - 1101750). Its height is the MEAN of the samples whose position lies in [E - 1500, E + 1500) x [N - 1500, N + 1500) (nine at this fixture's 1000 m cell, as the village has 25 at 10 m and 50 m spacing): sum_cm, the sum of their heights in whole centimetres, divided once in float64 by 100 x samples, minus 1250.25, rounded once to float32; a vertex strictly inside the area box is NaN (the quiet NaN 0x7FC00000, bytes 00 00 c0 7f). The 1000 m cells put samples on the squares' edges, as the village's 10 m samples at 50 m spacing do (design §0): the half-open rule is decided here. Computed by the pin author two independent ways (the throwaway step; plain Python in Fractions from source.json), identical bytes. local_y is the float32 value written as a decimal exactly.
